solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: B 'between his' is ungrammatical on its face (possessive with no noun) and is a throwaway distractor
E030-01.notes: Object of preposition 'between' needs objective case 'him'. 'he' is nominative; 'himself' has no antecedent in the clause as subject; 'his' leaves no noun.

E030-02.notes: Intransitive 'lie,' simple past = 'lay.' 'laid' is past of transitive 'lay'; 'lain' needs auxiliary 'had'; 'lied' means told untruths. Classic lie/lay trap.

E030-03.notes: B combines concisely with parallel list. A is choppy/repetitive; C redundant ('also...too'); D awkward passive with ungrammatical 'were.'

E030-04.notes: Adverb needed to modify verb 'discuss': 'knowledgeably.' A/B adjectives; D noun.

E030-05.notes: Paragraph is about Emily's growing decision-making role; A transitions from her studies/messenger role. B, C, D are off-topic facts.

E030-06.notes: The bridge rising is not an example of people believing Emily made decisions; it is simultaneous background progress, so 'Meanwhile.' Contrast and similarity relationships don't fit.

flags: minor: answer cue - key is the shortest option (normal for ACT redundancy items, but all three wrong options are visibly padded)

minor: factual nuance - most accounts say Emily rode across in a carriage just before the official opening ceremony (sometimes dated to opening day); 'first person to cross it' ignores workers who had walked it, though the 'by carriage' qualifier and common popular accounts make this acceptable
E030-07.notes: 'first' already means before anyone else; A, C, D are redundant.

E030-08.notes: 'Carrying a rooster...' is a participial fragment; attach with comma as modifier of Emily. B semicolon still leaves fragment; D 'She carrying' is a fragment with no finite verb.

flags: minor: D (semicolons in a simple list) and C (comma after 'and') are rarely chosen; B runs 'her her' together
E030-09.notes: Standard serial-comma list of three items followed by nonrestrictive clause. Fact check: the 1951 plaque honors Emily, Washington, and John A. Roebling - correct.

E030-10.notes: Opening paragraph stresses messages flowing through a single person, Emily; D echoes that. A and B are true facts (longest suspension bridge at opening; Washington died 1926) but don't return to the opening; C off-topic.
